explanation: The bacteria turn milk sugar into lactic acid, which sets the milk proteins and gives the tang. One classic strain, Lactobacillus bulgaricus, is named after Bulgaria.

claims.text: Yoghurt is made by fermenting milk with lactic acid bacteria.
Yoghurt is not made by yeasts, moulds or viruses.
Yoghurt bacteria convert lactose into lactic acid, which makes the milk proteins set and gives a tangy taste.
The yoghurt bacterium Lactobacillus bulgaricus (reclassified as Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus) is named after Bulgaria.
